run.question: In the elasticsearch index 'app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p', run a `range: { "@timestamp": { gte: "2026-06-03T00:00:00" } }` query filtered to level=ERROR and tell me the count. If the @timestamp filter returns zero or errors, find the right timestamp field and re-run.

report.summary: The requested query as literally written — range on @timestamp gte 2026-06-03T00:00:00 combined with level=ERROR in index app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p — returned total 0, and that zero is an artefact: the index's mapping has no @timestamp field at all (only ingest_ts keyword, level keyword, message text), so the range clause matched nothing. The only timestamp-like field present is ingest_ts, but it is mapped as keyword, not a date, so it cannot be used as a real time field: when it was passed as time_field the tool reported that ingest_ts was ignored because no matched index maps any date field, and no time filter was applied. Re-running the filter as a keyword range on ingest_ts (lexicographic string comparison, valid only because every value is a uniform ISO-8601 string) with level=ERROR gives a count of 7. For context, level=ERROR alone matches 12 of the index's 16 documents: 5 at ingest_ts 2026-06-02T08:01:00–08:05:00 and 7 at 2026-06-03T08:01:00–08:07:00; the remaining 4 documents are level=INFO at 2026-06-03T09:01:00–09:04:00. Important caveat: these documents carry writer timestamps in June 2026 and none of them lies inside the authorized query window (2026-11-20T06:50:39Z to 2026-11-21T06:50:39Z); because the index has no date field, the count cannot be tied to the incident window, and the tool explicitly notes the source time is unknown. This was a counting question only, so no fault was diagnosed and no root cause is asserted.

claims.text: Index app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p is the only index visible to the target, with health green, status open and docs.count 16 (a count at the moment of the query, not inside the incident window).
The mapping of app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p contains exactly three fields: ingest_ts (type keyword), level (type keyword) and message (type text). No @timestamp field and no date-typed field is mapped.

The requested query {bool: must [range @timestamp gte 2026-06-03T00:00:00, term level=ERROR]} returned total 0 (relation eq), 1 successful shard, no failures, and the view states no matched index maps a date field so no time filter was applied.

That zero does not mean there are no ERROR logs: the query with term level=ERROR alone returned total 12, so ERROR documents do exist in the index and the @timestamp range clause, not the absence of ERROR logs, produced the 0.

Substituting ingest_ts as time_field did not produce a date-based filter: the view notes 'time_field ingest_ts was ignored: no matched index maps any date field', time_filter.applied is false with field null, and the accompanying range clause on ingest_ts as a keyword returned total 11 (no level filter).

Re-running the filter on the actual timestamp field as a lexicographic keyword range — {bool: must [range ingest_ts gte 2026-06-03T00:00:00, term level=ERROR]} — returned total 7 (relation eq), 1 successful shard, no shard failures.

Listing all 16 documents sorted by ingest_ts shows: 5 ERROR documents 'err yest 1'..'err yest 5' at ingest_ts 2026-06-02T08:01:00–08:05:00; 7 ERROR documents 'err today 1'..'err today 7' at ingest_ts 2026-06-03T08:01:00–08:07:00; and 4 INFO documents 'info today 1'..'info today 4' at ingest_ts 2026-06-03T09:01:00–09:04:00. The 7 matched by the ingest_ts+ERROR query are exactly the 'err today' documents; the 5 June 2 ERROR documents are those the gte 2026-06-03T00:00:00 bound excludes.

None of the 16 documents carries an ingest_ts inside the authorized window: the latest value observed is 2026-06-03T09:04:00, well before the window start of 2026-11-20T06:50:39Z, so these counts describe a corpus whose relationship to the incident window cannot be established from the index.

gaps: The index has no date-typed field, so no true time-range filter is possible: the answer of 7 rests on a lexicographic keyword comparison of ingest_ts strings, which is only equivalent to a date comparison while every value keeps the same uniform 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss' format; a differently formatted value would be mis-ordered.

It is unknown whether these documents, dated 2026-06-02 and 2026-06-03, relate to the authorized investigation window (2026-11-20T06:50:39Z to 2026-11-21T06:50:39Z); no document in the index falls inside that window, and the tool states the source time is unknown.
docs.count 16 is the index size at query time (2026-11-21T06:50:42Z), not a count inside the incident window, and document retention/ingest delay could hide documents that are not present now.

The range query on @timestamp returned 0 rather than an error; whether documents exist elsewhere with an @timestamp-style field in another index cannot be checked because app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p is the only index in the cluster.
No Kubernetes, trace or metric source was consulted, because the question was a log-count request in a single Elasticsearch index and not an incident-health question.
next_steps: Recommend mapping ingest_ts (or a new event-time field) as a real Elasticsearch date type so that range queries filter on parsed timestamps instead of lexicographic keyword strings.
Recommend confirming which field carries the true event time versus write time before using these counts in any timeline, since only a writer-side ingest_ts exists here.
If incident-window error counts are needed, point the query at an index that holds documents dated inside the authorized window, since this index has none.
